answer: When graders disagree by two points or more, the panel stops averaging and opens an escrow. A third grader, drawn at dawn from the eligible pool, rereads the answer and issues a binding score within the hour. The arbiter takes 1.5 credits; whichever original grader sits farther from that score forfeits the rest. A lazy grader handing threes to every knoll of easy answers gains nothing, since each inflated score raises the odds of a paid arbitration it usually loses. That escrow turns every echo of a careless grade into real cost, so the cheapest path is reading the text.
